column2: A colleague asks where you are working today. Explain that you are working at home today.
Someone asks where your brother lives. Tell them that he lives in Ghent.
Someone asks about your group's language-learning routine. Explain that you learn Dutch every day.
A woman enjoys preparing meals for her friends. Tell someone what she enjoys doing.
A colleague asks what you are checking. Explain that you are checking the order.
Someone asks when a lesson starts. Tell them it starts at nine o'clock.
Your group is deciding where and when to go on holiday. Explain that you are planning your holiday.
You are recounting yesterday's work. Tell someone that your colleague wrote a report yesterday.
You are recounting yesterday's search for a missing possession. Say that you looked for your keys yesterday.
You are describing how a man paid for something earlier. Explain that he paid with his card.
Some children are playing in a garden right now. Tell someone what the children are doing and where.
Someone checks whether an explanation makes sense to you. Say that you understand this explanation.
You tried a new soup at an earlier meal. Tell a friend what you tried.
You and your companions ate at a new restaurant earlier. Explain that your group tried a new restaurant.
Someone asks where a man worked yesterday. Explain that he worked at home yesterday.
You are recounting a woman's phone call. Say that she called her mother.
You are describing where your household lived in the past. Explain that you used to live in Ghent.
You are discussing an earlier dance. Say that you danced with your wife.
Someone asks when a meeting finished. Explain that it ended at five o'clock.
You are recounting work completed earlier. Explain that your colleague checked the stock.
Someone asks what you did yesterday. Say that you read a book yesterday.
You are discussing a woman's earlier shopping trip. Explain that she bought a new coat.
You are recalling a discussion with your companions. Explain that your group made plans for the weekend.
You have tested a new recipe while cooking. Tell a friend what you tried.
You and your companions have tasted the soup. Tell someone what your group tasted, rather than what you cooked.
A man has checked an order. Tell your colleague that he completed that check.
You have finished putting things away in your bedroom. Tell someone that you tidied your room.
A woman has finished cleaning the windows. Tell someone what she cleaned.
Your group has finished a bike ride lasting two hours. Say how long you cycled, without naming a destination.
You have returned home by bicycle. Tell someone that you cycled home.
Someone asks about a man's earlier departure. Explain that he left early.
A woman has phoned her mother. Tell someone what she did.
Your group has finished discussing a problem. Tell someone what you talked about.
Someone asks about a task already mentioned. Explain that you finished it yesterday.
The train has arrived at its scheduled time. Tell someone that it arrived on time.
You are recalling a past visit. Before the visitors arrived, you had already made the soup. Explain what was already done.
You are recalling a past meeting. Your group had already read the report before that meeting. Explain what you had done.
You are recalling a request made to a woman. Explain that she had already written the letter before that request.
You are recalling being asked to do homework. Explain that you had already done it before that request.
You are recounting arriving at a man's workplace. Explain that he had already gone home before your arrival.
You are recalling a trip. Explain that your group had left early, before a later event in the story.
You are recalling being reminded about the door. Explain that you had already locked it before the reminder.
You are recalling telling a woman some news. Explain that she had already heard it before you spoke.
You are recalling a waiter bringing a payment request. Explain that your group had already paid the bill before that moment.
You are recalling a woman's arrival. Explain that you had tidied the room before she came.
You reached the station too late earlier. Explain that the train had already departed when you arrived.
You are recalling a later discussion about a problem. Explain that a man had already solved it before that discussion.
The soup is available to taste, and you would like to try it. Tell the person serving it what you want to do.
The door cannot be left open. Speaking for your group, explain that you must close it.
A man will be unable to attend tomorrow. Tell someone that he cannot come tomorrow.
A woman has permission to leave her car in this location. Explain that she is allowed to park here.
You are speaking for your group to someone awaiting a call. Promise that you will phone them tomorrow.
Someone asks what your group would like to do. Explain that you want to practise together.
A man is looking for different employment. Explain that he wants to find a new job.
You cannot guarantee you will fall asleep. Tell someone that you will try to sleep.
A leak needs attention, but success is uncertain. Promise that your group will try to repair the leak.
A task must be completed tomorrow. Tell the person responsible that they have to finish it tomorrow.
You are offering someone a taste of the soup in front of you. Ask whether they want to try this soup.
You would like to taste the dish in front of you. Ask permission to try this dish.
You need assistance from someone you address formally. Politely ask whether they can help you.
You want to arrange a meeting with a friend tomorrow. Suggest meeting tomorrow.
A friend has a task to finish, but you do not know the deadline. Ask whether they have to finish it tomorrow.
You are about to pay. Ask permission to pay by bank card.
You are looking at a coat in a shop. Ask whether you can try the coat on.
You are checking what another person wants to do. Ask whether they want to close the door.
You want to buy bread, but do not know where. Ask someone where you can buy it.
You have a lesson to attend and need its starting time. Ask what time the lesson begins.
You are pointing to a coat in a shop. Ask how much this coat costs.
You are getting to know someone's family. Ask where their brother lives.
Someone has arrived late. Ask them why they are late.
You are offering someone a drink. Ask what they want to drink.
The door has been closed, but you do not know by whom. Ask who closed it.
You are discussing today's work arrangements with a colleague. Ask whether they are working at home today.
Someone has mentioned a man whose address you are unsure of. Ask whether he lives in Ghent.
An item is too large. Politely ask a shop assistant whether they have a smaller size.
You are receiving a visitor formally. Ask whether they have an appointment.
A task has been discussed and may now be finished. Ask whether the other person has finished it yet.
Zoë may be buying an old car. Ask the person you are addressing whether they are selling the old car to her.
You need to visit a shop on a Monday. Ask whether the shop is open on Mondays.
Your friend wants to sell their old car, and Zoë wants to buy it. Tell your friend directly to sell their old car to Zoë.
You are offering someone a dish to taste. Encourage them directly to try this dish.
Someone has left their bedroom untidy. Tell that person to tidy their room by putting things away.
The windows are dirty. Tell another person to clean the windows.
Someone is holding a letter and other people need to hear it. Tell that person to read the letter aloud.
The person you are addressing is holding a book. Tell them to give the book to their brother.
Another person has an item that you need sent to you. Tell them directly to send it to you.
Someone is due to attend tomorrow. Tell them to arrive on time tomorrow.
Someone missed a call from the dentist. Tell that person to call the dentist back.
Someone is leaving a door unlocked. Tell them to lock the door.
You and a friend need practice. Suggest practising together.
You would like a coffee with your companion. Suggest having a cup of coffee together.
You and your companions are choosing where to eat. Suggest trying a new restaurant together.
The meeting time no longer works. Suggest that your group reschedule the meeting.
Your group needs a time to meet someone. Suggest making an appointment together.
Your group has several offers to consider. Suggest comparing the prices together.
You and your companions are ready to leave. Suggest going home together.
The room needs fresh air. Suggest that your group open the window.
You and a friend are deciding what to do. Suggest taking a walk together.
Your group has not organised its holiday yet. Suggest planning your holiday together.
A problem needs discussion. Suggest that your group discuss the problem together.
Your group will stop working for today. Suggest continuing tomorrow.
Someone asks what a man is doing right now. Explain that he is cooking.
Someone asks what you are doing in the kitchen right now. Explain that you are making the soup.
Someone asks what your group is studying right now. Explain that you are learning Dutch.
A woman is occupied with a book right now. Describe her as reading a book.
A man is cleaning the windows at this moment. Describe what he is doing.
Your manager is phoning your group right now. Tell someone who is calling you.
You are describing an activity interrupted earlier. Explain that you were tidying your room at that time.
You are recalling a wait at a station with your companions. Explain that your group was waiting for the train.
A man is washing his own clothes right now. Tell someone what he is doing.
You are describing a woman's activity at an earlier moment. Explain that she was writing a report.
Your group is preparing the table for a meal right now. Explain what you are doing.
Someone asks what is occupying a man right now. Explain that he is busy cooking.
A man is occupied with laundry tasks. Explain that he is busy with the laundry, without specifying one particular washing action.
A woman is occupied with cleaning the windows right now. Explain what she is busy doing.
Someone asks what is occupying you. Explain that you are busy writing a letter.
Your group is arranging its holiday right now. Explain that you are busy planning your holiday.
You are recalling what occupied a man earlier. Explain that he was busy tidying his room.
You are recalling a woman's activity at an earlier moment. Explain that she was busy cooking.
Someone asks what is keeping you occupied. Explain that you are busy with your homework.
Your group is occupied with reading a report right now. Explain what you are busy doing.
A man has finished reading the book. Tell someone that he is finished with that reading task.
Tidying up is a woman's assigned responsibility. Explain what she is responsible for.
You are making an effort to fall asleep right now. Explain that you are trying to sleep.
A man is making an effort to learn Dutch. Explain what he is trying to learn, without claiming that he already speaks it well.
Your group attempted to open a door earlier. Explain what you tried to do, without claiming success.
You cannot promise a successful call, but will make the attempt. Tell someone you will try to call.
Someone asks why you came here. Explain that you are here to help the person you are addressing.
A woman is prepared to leave now. Tell someone that she is ready to depart.
Someone thinks punctuality does not matter. Explain that arriving on time is important.
A task still needs completing, and your schedule allows it. Explain that you have time to finish it.
Your group intends to participate in an activity already discussed. Explain your group's plan to take part.
A man is asking you to return a phone call. Tell someone what he is asking you to do.
Someone asks what you would enjoy doing now. Explain that you feel like going outside.
Someone wants an explanation of a matter already discussed. Explain that explaining that is difficult.
Someone asks about a man's usual cleaning task. Explain that he cleans the windows.
A customer is waiting for a return phone call. Speaking for your group, explain that you call the customer back.
A woman has finished cleaning the kitchen. Tell someone what she cleaned.
Your group is preparing for an outing. Explain that you take water with you.
A man arrived with a book he brought along. Tell someone what he brought with him.
Your bedroom is untidy, but you have enough time to deal with it. Explain that you have time to tidy the room.
You are recalling a woman's participation in a meeting. Explain that she attended the meeting, rather than organised it.
Someone asks about your group's involvement in a course. Explain that you participate in that course.
Someone asks how you feel today. Tell them that you feel good today.
A man says he lacks energy. Tell someone that he feels tired.
Your group has been warmly received. Explain that you feel welcome.
You are recalling a woman's anxious state. Explain that she was worried.
You do not know where a man is and are thinking about it. Say that you wonder where he is.
Your group does not know the train's arrival time. Explain that you wonder when it will arrive.
A man still remembers what you are called. Tell someone that he remembers your name.
Someone mentions a day from the past. Explain that you remember that day.
You are speaking to several people moving quickly because they are short of time. Tell them that they are hurrying.
A woman is telling new acquaintances who she is. Describe her as introducing herself.
You have reliable information about a man's well-being. Say that you know he feels good.
You are ill and have decided not to go out. Explain that you are staying home because you are ill.
A man's visit is scheduled for tomorrow and you know about it. Say that you know he is coming tomorrow.
Someone asks when you practise Dutch. Explain that you practise if you have time.
You are recounting arriving home earlier. Explain that you were tired when you got home.
A man reads at the same time as you cook. Describe both activities and their overlap.
Someone is waiting to hear from you. Promise to phone them as soon as you are home.
You are waiting for a train and will not leave this place before it arrives. Explain how long you are staying here.
You are unsure whether a woman is at home. Say that you wonder whether she is home.
It is raining, so your group has decided to remain indoors. Explain the rain as the reason for staying inside.
You think a man is able to explain a matter, but are not claiming certainty. Express that opinion.
Someone phoned you earlier while you were away. Explain that you were not home when they called.
A woman tells you about her work tomorrow. Report that she says she has to work tomorrow.
Someone asks what you are drinking today. Explain that today you are drinking coffee.
Someone asks about tomorrow's work arrangements. Explain that you are working at home tomorrow.
You moved to Roeselare last year and still live there. Explain when your residence there began.
Someone is looking at the table. Explain that there is a book lying on it.
Someone asks what you hear each morning. Explain that you hear birds singing every morning.
You are discussing yesterday's meal. Explain that you tried a new soup yesterday.
Your lesson ended and your group then practised together. Explain what you did after the lesson.
Someone needs a ticket and you are pointing to the place where it is sold. Explain that they can buy a ticket here.
Someone asks what you drank earlier. Say that you drank a glass of water.
Someone points something out that you can also see. Tell them that you see that too.
Your group has planned a visit to Ghent next week. Explain where you are going and when.
Someone asks what is on the table. Tell them that a book is lying there.
Someone asks what is on your desk. Explain that there are two cups standing on it.
Someone is looking for milk. Tell them that there is milk in the fridge.
Someone asks about the sky. Explain that there are no clouds.
Someone asks what is on your desk. Explain that a cup of coffee is standing there.
Someone asks about the decoration on a wall. Explain that a photo is hanging on it.
You are recalling what was on a chair earlier. Explain that a cat was sitting on it.
The ground shook earlier and the event is over. Tell someone that there has been an earthquake.
Someone asks whether any seating is available. Explain that three places are still free.
Someone is looking for bread in the area. Explain that there is a bakery in this street.
Someone asks you to take on another activity, but your schedule is full. Explain that you have no time.
Someone offers coffee for a woman who does not drink it. Explain that she does not drink coffee.
Someone assumes a man needs rest. Explain that he is not tired.
Your group is expected somewhere today, but cannot attend. Explain that you cannot come today.
Someone asks about a letter, but you have not read it. Explain that you did not read the letter.
You are discussing an earlier meal. Explain that a woman did not drink her own coffee.
Another person believes they must work tomorrow, but it is not required. Tell them that they do not have to work tomorrow.
Someone is about to park where parking is prohibited. Tell them that they are not allowed to park here.
Someone offers you tea, but you do not want to drink it. Explain your wish.
A cashier offers your group a bag you do not need. Explain that your group does not need a bag.
Someone asks where your group's car is. Explain that your car is outside.
Someone asks about the size of your household's home. Explain that your house is small.
Your group is checking several of its own budgets. Explain what you are checking.
You are pointing to a cup farther away. Tell the person you are addressing that it is their cup.
A woman arrived with her own book. Explain that she brought her book along.
A man has a meeting that begins shortly. Tell someone when his meeting starts.
Someone asks about your household's children. Explain that your children are learning Dutch.
Your group has a report and you have read it. Tell a colleague that you read your group's report.
A man wants to buy your friend's old car. Tell your friend directly to sell their old car to him.
You see a proposal that may belong to a woman. Ask whether this is her proposal.
You are tasting a new dish right now. Tell someone that you are trying a new dish.
You are eating the new dish and enjoy its taste. Describe the new dish as tasty.
Someone asks about a book farther away. Identify it as a red book.
You are comparing bags in a shop. Explain that the red bag is expensive.
Your household has a new home. Tell someone that your new house is big.
Someone asks about the size of a business you are showing them. Explain that this is a large company.
Someone asks about the atmosphere in the office. Explain that the office is quiet.
The size you found is too large. Tell a shop assistant that you are looking for a smaller size.
You are discussing a woman's earlier shopping. Say that she bought a beautiful coat.
Your group has finished eating bread rolls and enjoyed them. Explain that you ate tasty rolls.
You are identifying a woman for someone. Explain that this is the woman who lives in Ghent.
The person you are addressing gave you a book earlier. Explain that you are now reading the book they gave you.
Some people are standing outside and waiting for a bus. Explain what the people standing outside are waiting for.
Someone asks what music you listen to. Explain that you listen to songs you like.
You are pointing out a particular house farther away. Identify it as the house next to the park.
A pen was lying on the table earlier, but is missing now. Explain that you are looking for that pen.
A man bought a coat yesterday and is wearing it now. Explain which coat he is wearing.
You are pointing out a dish that you tried earlier. Identify it as the dish you tried.
A colleague is helping your group and speaks Dutch. Explain that the colleague helping you speaks Dutch.
You need to complete a form, but cannot find it. Ask where the form you have to fill in is.
A woman knows the man who works at a place being pointed out. Explain which man she knows.
Your search for some keys was successful. Explain that you found the keys you were looking for.
Someone asks who is buying a printer you are selling. Explain that you are selling it to your colleague.
Someone asks whose words you listen to. Explain that you listen to your mother.
A man is waiting for a train right now. Tell someone what he is waiting for.
A woman enjoys reading very much. Tell someone that she loves reading.
Your group is discussing a meeting right now. Tell someone what you are talking about.
You are at a wedding and dancing. Tell someone what you are doing at that event.
Someone asks where you are right now. Explain that you are at the office.
Someone asks where you will go tomorrow. Explain that you are going to the office tomorrow.
Someone asks about your plans after work. Explain that you are going home after work.
Someone asks where the photo is. Explain that it hangs on the wall.
Someone asks where a man is sitting. Explain that he is sitting in the room.
Someone asks how you are seeking assistance. Explain that you ask your colleague for help.
Someone asks about your favourite pastime. Explain that reading is your hobby.
Someone thinks a kitchen can be cleaned instantly. Explain that cleaning the kitchen takes time.
Someone asks why you study Dutch. Explain that learning Dutch is important to you.
You are enjoying preparing a meal with someone. Explain that cooking together is fun.
Someone asks about an activity you love. Explain that you love reading outdoors.
A man is occupied with washing the windows right now. Explain what he is busy doing.
You are speaking affectionately to someone. Explain that thinking of them makes you happy.
Someone asks how difficult organising the trip is. Explain that planning the trip is easy.
You are recalling a woman's earlier passion. Explain that singing was her passion at that time.
You have finished tidying your room. Explain that the tidying took one hour.
Someone asks about several rooms after cleaning. Explain that the rooms are clean.
You are showing someone your own home. Identify this as your house.
Someone has proposed an idea. Point back to it and describe it as a good idea.
You are recounting a woman's career development. Explain that she became a good doctor.
You expect tomorrow to involve many activities. Tell someone that tomorrow will be a busy day.
Someone was working on a task already mentioned. Ask whether they have finished it.
Someone asks who receives an object you are giving. Explain that you give it to a man already mentioned.
Someone asks for information you cannot share. Explain that you cannot tell it to them.
Someone asks about a man's call to you. Explain that he called you yesterday.
Your group has an item to send. Tell someone that you will send it tomorrow.
You arrived with a book belonging to the person you are addressing. Explain that you brought their book along.
You are discussing helpful advice your group received earlier. Explain that a woman gave your group good advice.
Someone does not understand a matter you know about. Explain that you want to explain it to them.
You are discussing a particular dish with someone. Ask whether they have already tried this dish.
You plan to choose a different dish tomorrow. Explain that you will try a different dish tomorrow.
You are not certain you can prepare the soup successfully. Tell someone that you will try to make the soup.
A woman is tasting or testing the sauce at this moment. Tell someone that she is trying the sauce.
Your group has tested a different method. Explain that you tried a different approach.
You moved to Roeselare last year and still live there. Explain how long your residence there has continued.
You started working in Brussels in September and still work there. Explain when your work there began.
A man started learning Dutch in January and is still learning it. Explain when his learning began.
You have finished a two-hour cycling activity. Say how long you cycled, without specifying a destination.
Your group's wait has ended after ten minutes. Explain how long you waited.
Someone asks when the lesson begins. The starting time is 5:30. Tell them when it starts in Dutch.
Someone asks about your group's weekly work schedule. Explain that you work three days per week.
The train is running ten minutes behind schedule. Explain the length of its delay.
You arrived here one hour ago and are still here. Explain how long you have already been here.
A meeting's cancellation is taking place now. Tell someone that the meeting is being cancelled.
Someone is completing a form right now. Describe the form as being filled in, without naming the person doing it.
The form is complete now. Tell someone that the form has been filled in.
Someone is cleaning the windows right now. Describe the windows as being cleaned, without naming the cleaner.
You are recounting an earlier event. Explain that the door was closed, without naming who closed it.
You are discussing an earlier decision. Explain that the proposal was accepted, without naming the decision-maker.
The order's confirmation is complete. Tell someone that the order has been confirmed.
Inspectors are checking tickets right now. Describe the tickets as being checked, without naming the inspectors.
The difficulty has been resolved now. Explain that the problem has been solved.
You are discussing a letter sent earlier. Explain that it was sent yesterday, without naming who sent it.
You can hear birds singing right now. Tell someone what you hear the birds doing.
A woman can hear children playing. Tell someone what she hears the children doing.
Your group can see a train arriving. Explain what you see the train doing.
You watched a man go outside earlier. Explain what you saw him do.
A man heard someone making a call earlier. Explain what he heard someone doing.
Your group can hear a woman speaking Dutch. Explain what you hear her doing.
You can see children dancing. Explain what you see the children doing.
A woman watched a cat walk away earlier. Explain what she saw the cat do.
You can hear your male neighbour laughing. Explain what you hear him doing.
Your group watched a bus leave earlier. Explain what you saw the bus do.
A man can hear a dog barking. Explain what he hears the dog doing.
You watched a woman close the door earlier. Explain what you saw her do.
You want to write something but lack a pen. Explain that you need a pen.
Your group's available time is insufficient. Explain that you need more time.
A man cannot travel without his passport. Explain that he needs his passport.
You are recounting a woman's earlier difficulty. Explain that she needed help.
Your group managed an earlier journey without a map. Explain that you did not need a map.
You have a task tomorrow requiring your laptop. Explain that you will need your laptop tomorrow.
Another person may need a ticket. Ask whether they need one.
Your group faces a problem without an answer. Explain that you need a solution.
A man is unsure what to do and needs helpful guidance. Explain that he needs good advice.
You cannot continue without a little water. Explain that you need some water.
Someone asks where you are sitting. Explain that you are sitting on the chair.
You are about to take a seat on the sofa. Tell someone that you are going to sit down on the sofa.
You have taken a seat on the sofa. Explain that you sat down on the sofa.
Someone asks where a man is standing. Explain that he is standing by the bus stop.
You are recalling where a woman was resting earlier. Explain that she was lying on the bed.
You are standing while waiting for the bus right now. Describe yourself as waiting for the bus.
You are recounting a man's earlier wait. Explain that he was standing and waiting by the entrance.
A woman is seated and reading a book. Describe what she is doing while seated.
Someone wants your group to move, but you will not. Explain that you remain standing here.
Someone asks where the car is parked. Explain that the car is outside.
You have finished a one-hour wait spent sitting. Explain what you did and how long you waited.
Someone has completed a task successfully. Congratulate them with a short expression meaning well done.
You are ordering at a café. Politely ask for one cup of coffee.
You are ordering at a bakery. Politely ask for two bread rolls.
You are leaving someone whom you will see tomorrow. Say goodbye with that next meeting in mind.
Someone is about to attempt something important. Wish them good luck.
Someone worries that a small request inconveniences you. Reassure them that it is no problem.
Someone offers you help. Tell them, informally, that their gesture is kind.
You have kept someone waiting longer than expected. Apologise specifically for the delay.
You are leaving a colleague before the weekend. Wish them a pleasant weekend.
You are pointing to a book near you. Tell someone that this book is interesting.
You are pointing to a bag near you. Tell someone that this bag is expensive.
You are pointing to a house farther away. Tell someone that that house is big.
Someone asks about a particular car farther away. Explain that that car is outside.
You are pointing to several books near you. Explain that these books are new.
You are pointing to some people farther away. Explain that those people live here.
You are choosing bread at a shop. Point to bread near you and say that you want this bread.
You have chosen the coat near you. Tell the assistant that you will take this coat.
You are discussing a particular dish farther away or previously mentioned. Ask whether the other person has tried that dish.
You are pointing to a car farther away. Tell someone that it is your group's car.
